analysis.investment_thesis: CLN Energy fails both Magic Formula tests — earnings yield of ~3.9% (P/E 25.4) is far below my 12% threshold, and ROCE of 12.25% falls short of the 20%+ I require for a "good" business. Cheap-and-good this is not; it's expensive-and-mediocre on the numbers presented.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 72.6% signals insider skin-in-the-game
Exposure to EV powertrain/battery theme with secular tailwinds
FII stake of 12.6% suggests some institutional validation
key_risks: ROCE 12.25% is sub-par for a capital-intensive manufacturing business
Earnings yield ~3.9% is deeply overvalued on Magic Formula criteria
Tiny Rs 296 Cr market cap with 2019 vintage — unproven cycle-tested economics
red_flags: ROCE < 15% in a capital-hungry lithium-ion/motor manufacturing business
P/E 25.4 implies earnings yield well below risk-free rate in India
Auto-component/EV battery space is capex-heavy — risk of ROCE compression as capacity scales
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula is brutally simple: I want high earnings yield AND high return on capital. CLN Energy delivers neither. At a P/E of 25.4, earnings yield sits around 3.9% — you'd earn more in an Indian government bond with no business risk. ROCE of 12.25% is below the cost of capital for a small-cap manufacturer and well under my 20% hurdle. Ranked against the Indian universe, this would land in the bottom quartile on both axes simultaneously — the worst possible quadrant in my framework.

The EV battery narrative is seductive, but narratives don't feature in the formula. A capital-intensive lithium-ion and motor manufacturer needs either dominant scale economics or proprietary chemistry to earn >20% on incremental capital, and there is no evidence here of either. Until ROCE inflects above 20% AND the valuation compresses to a double-digit earnings yield, this is a pass. I'd revisit only if the price halved or earnings roughly tripled while capital efficiency improved.
